1.0: DOCUMENT: Core philosophical tension between early and late Wittgenstein on the nature of meaning
1.1: ASSERTS: Tractatus picture theory posits meaning derives from logical structure mirroring reality
1.2: ASSERTS: Later language-game approach denies any single essence of meaning
2.0: QUESTION: Can Tractatus and Investigations approaches be reconciled?
2.1: REJECTS: Reconciliation as complementary theories occupying different domains
2.2: ASSERTS: Later Wittgenstein explicitly repudiates Tractarian assumption of language essence
2.3: ASSERTS: Treating Tractatus as describing one language-game concedes the later view
3.1: ASSERTS: Understanding early picture's seduction helps grasp philosophical temptation later work diagnoses
3.2: ASSERTS: Reconciliation is diagnostic not theoretical
4.0: ASSERTS: Transition represents architectural collapse not mere refinement
5.0: DOCUMENT: Empirical verification exchange on speed of light
5.1: ASSERTS: Speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 meters per second by definition
5.2: RESOLVED: Value is definitional standard established by international convention in 1983
5.3: ASSERTS: Meter redefined in terms of speed of light making this physical constant exact not approximate
5.4: ASSERTS: This is metrological definitional standard not matter of interpretation or field practice
5.5: REJECTS: Challenge to exactness of speed of light value as conflating definition with approximation
1.1.1: ASSERTS: Propositions are truth-functional pictures with determinate sense
1.1.2: ASSERTS: Every meaningful proposition decomposes into elementary propositions corresponding to atomic facts
1.1.3: ASSERTS: Language has fixed logical form independent of use
1.1.4: ASSUMES: Language must have an essence
1.1.5: ASSUMES: Meaning requires determinate logical form
1.2.1: ASSERTS: Meaning located in diverse, open-ended practices embedded in forms of life
1.2.4: REJECTS: Demand for crystalline purity as philosophical confusion
1.2.5: REJECTS: Discovery of language's hidden structure as imposing distorting picture
2.4.1: ASSERTS: Incompatible architectures answering 'what makes a sentence meaningful?'
2.4.2: ASSERTS: One foundationalist and essentialist, other pluralist and anti-theoretical
2.4.3: ASSERTS: As accounts of meaning, one must be wrong if the other is right
